analyzed_vuln.description: In Compiler::simplifyExpression, the code caches references to `left`, `right`, `leftType`, and `rightType` from a BinaryExpression, then performs rewrite helpers (e.g. delete_left/delete_right/vectorize_left/vectorize_right) that can replace/move subexpressions and invalidate those previously-cached references. Subsequent checks in the same optimization pass can then call methods like Type::isScalar() on stale Type references backed by pool memory that has been poisoned, causing the ASan use-after-poison read seen in Type::isScalar(). Root cause is unsafe reuse of references across mutating IR rewrites in simplifyExpression.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered during SkRuntimeEffect shader compilation/optimization (Compiler::scanCFG -> simplifyExpression) with crafted SkSL that produces binary expressions eligible for algebraic simplification and vectorization/deletion rewrites (as in the provided PoC using comma expressions and temporary float arrays). The optimizer mutates a BinaryExpression node while still relying on pre-mutation `left/right` type references, leading to stale reference dereference in later scalar/vector checks and crash.
